newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on concerns of new PM.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on concerns of new PM.

text.p: Muted concern to the prospect of Thai Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh securing the premiership took its toll on the stock market which retreated from a 16-point morning rally to end the day sharply lower.

The SET index hit an intraday peak of 1,061.91 five minutes after opening before it lapsed into the negative territory shortly after the market resumed in the afternoon. It ended the day down 11.01 points at 1,034.37 on moderate 4.8 billion baht turnover.
"Investors sold on concerns that Chavalit would be appointed new prime minister," said Bumnan Liumsuwan of Asia Credit.

Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa announced on Saturday that he would step down within seven days in exchange for support of five coalition partners to help him win a no-confidence vote in parliament.
Chavalit, leader of New Aspiration Party, has been tipped as the front runner to succeed Banharn.
"Investors are sceptical that Chavalit, if appointed, could solve economic problems and that's why they decided to sell and take profits," said Bumnan.
All counters closed lower except finance and printing sectors which gained 0.09 percent and 1.9 percent respectively.
Finance One topped the active list, falling 0.50 baht to 99, and Thai Farmers Bank slipped three to 167.
Among the top losers, Land and Houses dipped 2.75 baht to 25.50, and Kulthorn Kirby lost four to 38.
"The index is expected to continue falling tomorrow as investors are still waiting for a new prime minister to be named," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
Market support is seen at 1,030 on Tuesday against a resistance at 1,055, brokers said.
